outputs.L1: Method and device for determining at least one substance concentration (c), or at least one substance, in a liquid medium, wherein the method comprises the following steps: introducing the liquid medium into a vessel of known shape at a predefined flow speed; coupling electromagnetic waves having a predefined wavelength or a predefined wavelength range into the liquid medium contained in the vessel, wherein the electromagnetic waves travel along a path length in the liquid medium that is dependent on a fill level (xi) of the liquid medium in the vessel; measuring intensities (Φi) of the electromagnetic waves after they have traveled the path length in the liquid medium at at least two predefined points in time (ti) and/or at at least two predefined fill levels (xi) of the vessel; and, after a final intensity measurement, determining the at least one substance concentration (c), or the at least one substance, using the measured intensities (Φi) and the at least two predefined points in time (ti) or the at least two predefined fill levels (xi), respectively.
outputs.L2: A method and apparatus are provided for identifying at least one substance and/or determining at least one substance concentration (c) in a liquid medium. The method includes introducing the liquid medium into a vessel of known geometry at a predetermined flow rate. Electromagnetic radiation with a specified wavelength, or within a specified wavelength range, is directed into the liquid medium inside the vessel. The radiation travels through the liquid medium over a distance that depends on the fill level (xi) of the liquid medium in the vessel. After passing through this distance in the liquid medium, the intensities (Φi) of the electromagnetic radiation are recorded at no fewer than two predetermined times (ti) and/or at no fewer than two predetermined vessel fill levels (xi). Once the final intensity measurement has been taken, the measured intensities (Φi), together with the at least two predetermined times (ti) or the at least two predetermined fill levels (xi), are used to determine the at least one substance concentration (c) or to identify the at least one substance.

The method is used to determine the concentration of at least one substance in a liquid medium and/or to identify at least one substance contained in the liquid medium. For this purpose, the liquid medium is introduced into a vessel having a known shape or geometry. The liquid medium is supplied to the vessel at a predefined flow speed, so that the fill level of the vessel changes in a known or determinable manner over time.

Electromagnetic waves having a predefined wavelength or a predefined wavelength range are coupled into the liquid medium located in the vessel. The selected wavelength or wavelength range is preferably chosen such that the substance to be detected or quantified has a characteristic absorption, transmission, reflection, scattering, or other optical interaction within that spectral range.

As the liquid medium fills the vessel, the electromagnetic waves propagate through the liquid over a path length that depends on the current fill level of the vessel. Because the vessel geometry and the flow speed are known, the optical path length through the liquid medium can be assigned to a particular time or fill level. Thus, during the filling process, a plurality of intensity measurements can be obtained at different times and/or different fill levels, corresponding to different path lengths through the liquid.

The measured intensities are evaluated to determine the concentration and/or identity of the substance. In particular, changes in intensity as a function of the optical path length may be analyzed. The evaluation may be based on absorption behavior, for example using the Beer-Lambert law, or on another wavelength-dependent interaction between the electromagnetic waves and the substance. By comparing the measured intensity values, or values derived therefrom, with reference data, calibration data, or characteristic spectral signatures, the method enables reliable determination of the concentration of at least one substance and/or identification of at least one substance present in the liquid medium.
outputs.L4:
A method and a corresponding device are provided for determining the concentration of a substance in a liquid, or for identifying a substance contained in a liquid, by means of optical measurement. The liquid to be analyzed is introduced into a vessel having a known geometry. The liquid is supplied to the vessel at a known flow speed or at a flow rate from which the increase in fill level over time can be determined. As the vessel fills, the optical path length through the liquid changes in a predictable manner, because the distance traveled by electromagnetic radiation through the liquid depends on the instantaneous fill level and on the shape and dimensions of the vessel.

During filling, electromagnetic waves, for example light in the visible, ultraviolet, or infrared range, are directed through the vessel and through the liquid contained therein. The radiation passes through the liquid along optical paths whose lengths vary as the fill level changes. At two or more different times, or at two or more corresponding fill levels, the intensity of the radiation transmitted through the liquid is measured by a detector. The measured transmitted intensities are therefore associated with different known or determinable path lengths through the liquid.

The resulting measurement data are evaluated together with the corresponding times, fill levels, or path lengths. Since the attenuation of electromagnetic radiation passing through a liquid depends on the optical path length and on the absorption or scattering properties of the substance present in the liquid, the change in transmitted intensity as a function of path length can be used to derive information about the liquid. In particular, the concentration of a known substance may be calculated from the measured intensities using an absorption relationship such as the Beer-Lambert law. Alternatively, the measured intensity pattern at one or more wavelengths may be compared with reference data in order to identify an unknown substance or to distinguish between different possible substances.

The device may include a vessel of predetermined shape, an inlet for introducing the liquid into the vessel at a known or controlled flow speed, a source of electromagnetic radiation arranged to direct radiation through the vessel, and one or more detectors arranged to measure the intensity of radiation transmitted through the liquid. The device may further include a control and evaluation unit configured to record the transmitted intensities at different times or fill levels, determine the corresponding optical path lengths from the known vessel geometry and filling behavior, and calculate the substance concentration or identify the substance on the basis of the recorded data.

Because the optical path length is varied by the filling process itself, the method does not require multiple cuvettes or mechanically adjustable optical paths. Instead, a single vessel with known geometry can provide a range of effective path lengths as the liquid level changes. This enables a compact and comparatively simple optical analysis arrangement. By measuring transmitted intensities at different path lengths, the reliability of the concentration determination or substance identification can be improved, and measurements can be adapted to liquids having different absorption strengths or concentration ranges.

## Method

A **method** is a structured way of doing something. It provides a clear process, a set of steps, or a system that helps people achieve a specific goal. Whether in science, education, business, or everyday life, using a method makes tasks more organized, efficient, and reliable.

In research, a method explains how information is collected, analyzed, and interpreted. A strong research method helps ensure that results are accurate and trustworthy. In learning, a method can refer to a teaching strategy or study technique that helps students understand new ideas more effectively. In business, a method may be used to improve productivity, solve problems, or manage projects.

The value of a good method lies in its consistency. When a method is clearly defined, it can be repeated, tested, and improved over time. This makes it easier to identify what works well and what needs to change. A method also helps reduce confusion because everyone involved understands the process and their role within it.

Choosing the right method depends on the goal, the available resources, and the situation. Some methods are simple and practical, while others are more detailed and technical. The best method is one that fits the task and leads to useful, dependable results.

In short, a method is more than just a way of working. It is a tool for creating order, improving outcomes, and turning ideas into action.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a method and device that determines substance concentration in a liquid by measuring attenuation of electromagnetic waves at different fill levels in a vessel.
counterfactuals.output: A method and device are provided for determining a concentration of a substance in a liquid contained in a vessel. Electromagnetic waves are transmitted through or into the vessel at a plurality of liquid fill levels, and corresponding attenuation values are measured for each fill level. A relationship between attenuation and fill level is evaluated to distinguish attenuation caused by the liquid path length from attenuation attributable to the substance. Based on the evaluated relationship, a concentration value of the substance in the liquid is determined. The device may include an electromagnetic transmitter, a receiver arranged to detect attenuated waves after interaction with the liquid, a fill-level sensor or level-determining unit, and a processing unit configured to associate measured attenuation values with respective fill levels and calculate the substance concentration. The method enables concentration determination with reduced dependence on vessel geometry, sensor offset, or fixed calibration conditions.
